rules.title: Environments are segregated
rules.noncompliance: The same credential or production endpoint appears in development, test and production configuration, or production values are committed alongside development ones.
rules.remediation: Give each environment its own identity, secrets and network; keep production values out of the repository and inject them at deploy time.
rules.keywords: environments segregated production development separate access

requirement.statement: Development, testing, staging and production environments are segregated.
Applications and workloads use unique credentials that are not shared with other applications or workloads, or across development, testing, staging and production environments.

guidance.quote: Ensure that user, machine, system and service account credentials are unique per system or account, particularly in high-privilege contexts.
guidance.title: essentials essentials for enterprise it__2.xlsx
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

rules.title: Software artefacts are tested for known weaknesses
rules.noncompliance: Continuous integration builds and ships the software without a SAST, DAST or software composition analysis step.
rules.remediation: Add SAST and dependency (SCA) scanning to the pipeline and make findings above an agreed severity fail the build; keep the results as assessment evidence.
rules.keywords: static analysis vulnerability scanning dependencies testing known weaknesses

requirement.statement: All software artefacts are tested to detect known weaknesses using static application security testing (SAST), dynamic application security testing (DAST) or software composition analysis (SCA), depending on the software artefact type, before being imported into the authoritative source for software.

rules.title: Third-party components come from trustworthy sources
rules.noncompliance: Dependencies are fetched from raw URLs, unpinned git branches or extra package indexes, or build steps pipe downloaded scripts to a shell.
rules.remediation: Use a controlled internal or vetted registry as the authoritative source, verify hashes or signatures, and avoid fetch-and-execute build steps.
rules.keywords: trusted sources third-party components libraries provenance integrity

requirement.statement: The authoritative source for software restricts the use and import of third-party libraries and software components to trustworthy sources.

rules.title: Dependencies are pinned to approved versions
rules.noncompliance: Dependency manifests use ranges, wildcards or 'latest', base images use floating tags, or no lockfile is committed.
rules.remediation: Commit lockfiles, pin exact versions (and image digests), and change versions through reviewed updates.
rules.keywords: pin dependencies versions lockfile reproducible build

requirement.statement: Software artefact dependencies are pinned to approved versions in source code.

rules.title: A software bill of materials is produced
rules.noncompliance: No SBOM generation step or SBOM artefact was found for software that is delivered to others.
rules.remediation: Generate an SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) in the release pipeline and publish it with the artefact.
rules.keywords: software bill of materials SBOM components inventory

requirement.statement: A software bill of materials is produced and made available to consumers of software.

guidance.quote: Inventory information includes, for example, hardware inventory specifications, software license information, software version numbers, component owners, and – for networked components or devices – machine names and network addresses.
guidance.title: csrc nist gov pubs sp 800 161 r1 upd1 final

rules.title: Third-party SBOMs are used during development
rules.noncompliance: Imported components are not checked against their SBOMs or known-vulnerability data during development.
rules.remediation: Ingest supplier SBOMs where available and check components against vulnerability data in CI.
rules.keywords: software bill of materials third-party components vulnerabilities supplier

requirement.statement: If a software bill of materials is available for imported third-party software components, it is used during software development to ensure such software components have no known vulnerabilities.

rules.title: Input from the internet is validated and sanitised
rules.noncompliance: Request data reaches an interpreter (SQL, shell, eval) by string construction.
rules.remediation: Validate against a schema at the boundary, and use parameterised queries and argument vectors instead of string building.
rules.keywords: input validation sanitisation injection untrusted data parameterised

requirement.statement: Validation and sanitisation are performed on all input received over the internet by software.
The OWASP API Security Top 10 are mitigated in the development of web APIs.

rules.title: Serialised data is validated before deserialisation
rules.noncompliance: Untrusted data is deserialised with a format that can execute code (pickle, yaml.load, Java object streams).
rules.remediation: Use a data-only format with a schema (JSON), or a safe loader, and validate before parsing.
rules.keywords: deserialisation untrusted serialised data validation

requirement.statement: Data sources and serialised data inputs are validated before being deserialised.

rules.title: Web application output is encoded
rules.noncompliance: Templates or components disable auto-escaping or write raw HTML (innerHTML, |safe, dangerouslySetInnerHTML).
rules.remediation: Keep framework auto-escaping on, encode for the output context, and sanitise any HTML that must be rendered.
rules.keywords: output encoding cross-site scripting escaping html

requirement.statement: Output encoding is performed on all output produced by web applications.

rules.title: Session cookies set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite
rules.noncompliance: Session cookie configuration explicitly turns off HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite.
rules.remediation: Set all three flags by default; relax SameSite only with a documented reason.
rules.keywords: session cookies HttpOnly Secure SameSite

requirement.statement: If supported, web application session cookies set the HttpOnly flag, Secure flag and the SameSite flag by default.

rules.title: Security policy response headers are set
rules.noncompliance: A web application is present but no Content-Security-Policy, HSTS or X-Frame-Options configuration was found.
rules.remediation: Set Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security and X-Frame-Options in the web server or framework middleware.
rules.keywords: content security policy HSTS X-Frame-Options response headers

requirement.statement: Content-Security-Policy, Hypertext Transfer Protocol Strict Transport Security and X-Frame-Options are specified by web server software via security policy in response headers.

rules.title: Web content is offered only over HTTPS
rules.noncompliance: Configuration turns off HTTPS redirection or serves on plain HTTP.
rules.remediation: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS, set HSTS, and terminate TLS to current policy.
rules.keywords: HTTPS only web content redirect transport

requirement.statement: All web application content is offered exclusively using HTTPS.

rules.title: AI models are stored in non-executable formats
rules.noncompliance: Model artefacts are pickle-based (.pkl, .pt, .joblib) or loaded with arbitrary-code-execution options.
rules.remediation: Use safetensors or another non-executable format; load with weights_only or equivalent, and verify provenance.
rules.keywords: AI model files non-executable safetensors pickle arbitrary code

requirement.statement: AI models are stored in a non-executable file format that does not allow arbitrary code execution.

rules.title: AI model and system cards document the AI application
rules.noncompliance: The system uses AI models but no model card, system card or equivalent was found.
rules.remediation: Keep a model card and a system card (purpose, data, limits, architecture, risks) with the code.
rules.keywords: model cards system cards AI documentation characteristics

requirement.statement: AI-specific documentation, including AI model cards and AI system cards (or equivalent artefacts), is used to document AI model characteristics, system architectures, use cases and security risks.

rules.title: Exact model confidence scores are not exposed
rules.noncompliance: Log-probabilities or exact confidence values are returned through an API or user interface.
rules.remediation: Return bands or decisions, not exact scores; keep raw scores server-side.
rules.keywords: confidence scores logprobs model inversion extraction API outputs

requirement.statement: The exposure of exact AI model confidence scores in API outputs or user interfaces is prevented.

rules.title: Organisational data is not used to train AI without consent
rules.noncompliance: Code or documents describe fine-tuning or training on data the system collects from its users.
rules.remediation: Record informed, explicit consent for any such use, or exclude the data.
rules.keywords: training data consent fine-tuning organisational data AI

requirement.statement: Organisational data generated, collected or processed by AI applications is not used for training, fine-tuning or improving AI models unless informed and explicit consent has been obtained from data owners in advance.

guidance.quote: The exfiltration of training data can be a serious privacy concern for models that are trained on sensitive data, including data that contains personally identifiable information.
guidance.title: cyber gov au publication engaging with artificial intelligence
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

rules.title: AI agents are registered
rules.noncompliance: The system defines AI agents but no register (identifier, owner, purpose, identities, tools) was found.
rules.remediation: Maintain an AI agent register in the repository and verify it regularly.
rules.keywords: AI agent register inventory owner identities tools permissions

requirement.statement: An AI agent register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

An AI agent register contains the following for each AI agent:

- its unique identifier
- its owner and business purpose
- the identities assigned to it
- any user accounts and credentials it uses
- the tools, permissions and data repositories it can access.

rules.title: Agents are limited to the minimum tools and permissions
rules.noncompliance: An agent is given shell, arbitrary file or network tools with no human approval step or scoping.
rules.remediation: Give each agent only the tools its task needs, scope permissions per task, and require approval for destructive or external actions.
rules.keywords: agentic AI excessive agency least privilege tools permissions human approval

requirement.statement: Agentic AI applications are restricted to the minimum set of tools, functions and permissions required for their intended purpose.

Tools invoked by agentic AI applications are subject to both the access controls of the invoking user and agent-specific, task-scoped authorisation, with effective permissions limited to the minimum permitted by both.

rules.title: Workloads use short-lived, dynamically issued credentials
rules.noncompliance: Long-lived static access keys, tokens or private keys are present in code or configuration.
rules.remediation: Use workload identity (OIDC federation, instance or pod roles) and short-lived tokens instead of static keys.
rules.keywords: short-lived credentials workload identity federation tokens rotate

requirement.statement: Applications and workloads use short-lived dynamically issued credentials in preference to long-lived static credentials.

rules.title: Static credentials are held in a secrets manager
rules.noncompliance: Passwords, API keys or tokens are written into source, IaC or committed environment files.
rules.remediation: Move secrets to a secrets manager and read them at runtime; rotate anything that was committed.
rules.keywords: secrets management credentials storage vault rotation hardcoded

requirement.statement: Static credentials used by applications and workloads are centrally managed using a credential or secrets management solution.

rules.title: Credentials are unique per application and environment
rules.noncompliance: The same secret value is used in more than one environment or application.
rules.remediation: Issue distinct credentials per workload and environment.
rules.keywords: unique credentials not shared environments applications

requirement.statement: Applications and workloads use unique credentials that are not shared with other applications or workloads, or across development, testing, staging and production environments.

guidance.quote: Ensure that user, machine, system and service account credentials are unique per system or account, particularly in high-privilege contexts.
guidance.title: essentials essentials for enterprise it__2.xlsx
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

rules.title: Credentials are not stored in the clear
rules.noncompliance: Credentials or private keys are readable in files; a credentials scan would find them.
rules.remediation: Run a credential scan at least monthly and in CI; change any static credential found in the clear.
rules.keywords: credentials stored in the clear scan change compromised

requirement.statement: Systems are scanned at least monthly to identify any credentials that are being stored in the clear.

Static credentials used by applications and workloads are changed if:

- they are compromised or suspected of being compromised
- they are discovered stored on systems in the clear
- they are discovered being transferred across networks in the clear.

rules.title: Multi-factor authentication is used
rules.noncompliance: Identity provider or IaC configuration explicitly disables MFA.
rules.remediation: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all human users, and at minimum for privileged and remote access.
rules.keywords: multi-factor authentication phishing-resistant privileged remote access

requirement.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.
Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate privileged human users of systems.
Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate unprivileged human users of systems.

guidance.quote: In such a scenario, multi-factor authentication for remote access is significantly better than single-factor authentication but does not negate the requirement for appropriately hardened devices to be used as part of a comprehensive remote access solution.
guidance.title: cyber gov au publication implementing multi factor authentication
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

rules.title: Default credentials are changed
rules.noncompliance: Service configuration ships a well-known default or placeholder credential (admin/admin, postgres/postgres, changeme).
rules.remediation: Generate unique credentials at provisioning time and disable pre-configured accounts.
rules.keywords: default credentials changed disabled removed initial setup hardening

requirement.statement: Default user accounts or credentials for server applications, including for any pre-configured user accounts, are changed, disabled or removed during initial setup.
Default user accounts or credentials for operating systems, including for any pre-configured user accounts, are changed, disabled or removed during initial setup.

rules.title: Only the latest TLS version is used
rules.noncompliance: Configuration permits SSLv3, TLS 1.0 or 1.1 (or a minimum below TLS 1.2).
rules.remediation: Set the minimum to the latest supported version, with older versions disabled.
rules.keywords: TLS version configuration latest protocol disable

requirement.statement: Only the latest version of TLS is used for TLS connections.

rules.title: TLS uses approved cipher and key-establishment settings
rules.noncompliance: Configuration allows RC4, 3DES, CBC, NULL, EXPORT or anonymous suites, or enables TLS compression.
rules.remediation: Restrict to AES-GCM suites with ephemeral key establishment; disable compression.
rules.keywords: TLS cipher suites AES-GCM ephemeral key exchange perfect forward secrecy

requirement.statement: AES-GCM is used for encryption of TLS connections.
Anonymous DH is not used for TLS connections.
TLS compression is disabled for TLS connections.

rules.title: Network traffic is limited to what the business requires
rules.noncompliance: Security groups, firewall rules or storage policies admit the whole internet to administrative, database or storage endpoints.
rules.remediation: Deny by default; allow named sources and ports only; put administration behind a bastion or private access path.
rules.keywords: network segmentation firewall ingress restrict traffic least privilege

requirement.statement: Network access controls are implemented to limit the flow of network traffic within and between network segments to only that required for business purposes.
A software firewall is implemented on workstations and servers to restrict inbound and outbound network connections to an organisation-approved set of applications and services.

guidance.quote: Isolate systems within network zones based on business criticality and trust level, and restrict and monitor inbound and outbound access to explicitly approved pathways and services.
guidance.title: 2.xlsx [Boundary services]
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

guidance.quote: To reduce this risk, software-based firewalls that filter both incoming and outgoing traffic should be appropriately implemented.
guidance.title: cyber gov au publication hardening microsoft windows 10 workstations
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

rules.title: Event logs go to a centralised facility and are retained
rules.noncompliance: No log forwarding, central logging or retention configuration was found for a system that runs services.
rules.remediation: Forward event logs to a central facility promptly, protect them, and retain them searchably for at least twelve months.
rules.keywords: event logging centralised retention detection monitoring

requirement.statement: A centralised event logging facility is implemented.
Event logs sent to a centralised event logging facility are sent as soon as possible after they occur.
Event logs are retained in a searchable manner for at least 12 months.

rules.title: Updates for vulnerabilities are applied promptly
rules.noncompliance: No dependency or image update automation was found.
rules.remediation: Enable automated update proposals and set a patching timeframe that meets the ISM (48 hours when an exploit exists, otherwise two weeks for online services).
rules.keywords: patch updates vulnerabilities timeframe automation

requirement.statement: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

heuristics.title: Incident response plan exists and has been exercised
heuristics.concern: An assessor asks for the plan and evidence that it has been exercised, and that reporting to ASD is understood.
questions: Who is the incident owner and on-call contact?
When was the plan last exercised, and what changed afterwards?
Does it say when and how to report to ASD?
heuristics.evidence: The plan, an exercise record with actions closed, and the reporting procedure.

heuristics.title: A patching plan with evidence of operation
heuristics.concern: Patch timeframes in the ISM are specific; assessors look for the procedure and for records showing they were met.
questions: What are the patch timeframes by asset class?
Where is the record that the last critical patch met them?
heuristics.evidence: Patch procedure, patch report or dashboard export, and exceptions with risk acceptance.

heuristics.title: Vulnerability scanning with reviewed results
heuristics.concern: Scanning that nobody reads is not a control. Assessors ask for scan cadence and for what was done with results.
questions: How often are systems scanned?
Who reviews findings and where is the remediation tracked?
heuristics.evidence: Scan schedule, the last two reports, and remediation tickets.

guidance.quote: Vulnerability scanning usually entails using an automated vulnerability scanner to scan a host or groups of hosts on a network for application, network, and operating system vulnerabilities.
guidance.title: csrc nist gov pubs sp 800 45 ver2 final

heuristics.title: MFA on remote and administrative access
heuristics.concern: Absent or partial MFA on remote and privileged access is the first thing an assessor tests.
questions: Which access paths (VPN, console, SSH, CI/CD, break-glass) are covered?
Is the factor phishing-resistant?
heuristics.evidence: Identity provider policy export and a list of exemptions.

heuristics.title: Alerts from security tooling are actually watched
heuristics.concern: Tooling that generates alerts no one reads is a recurring assessment finding.
questions: Who triages alerts, and within what time?
What happens out of hours?
heuristics.evidence: Alert routing, on-call roster and a sample of triaged alerts.

heuristics.title: Firewall and egress rules restrict by default
heuristics.concern: Rules that allow any-any, or no egress control, are read as no boundary control.
questions: Is the default rule deny?
How are exceptions reviewed?
heuristics.evidence: Firewall or security-group rule export with owner and justification per rule.

heuristics.title: Credentials are not kept in files or code
heuristics.concern: Privileged passwords in files and scripts are a recurring failure; assessors ask how secrets are stored and scanned for.
questions: Where are production secrets stored?
Is there a scan for credentials in the clear, and how often?
heuristics.evidence: Secrets-manager configuration and the latest credential scan result.

guidance.quote: Identify and remediate unsecured keys, secrets and credentials by regularly scanning codebases, configuration files, file shares and user collaboration platforms.
guidance.title: essentials essentials for enterprise it__2.xlsx
guidance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Commonwealth of Australia, Australian Signals Directorate)

heuristics.title: AI agents have owners, permissions and tool scopes on record
heuristics.concern: Agentic services act with the permissions they are given; assessors ask who owns each agent and what it can do.
questions: Which agents exist, who owns each, and what tools can they call?
Which actions need human approval?
Is retrieved content treated as untrusted?
heuristics.evidence: AI agent register, tool permission matrix and approval flow description.

heuristics.title: Production data and credentials stay out of non-production
heuristics.concern: Copies of production data, or shared credentials, in development weaken the segregation the ISM requires.
questions: Is production data ever copied to development or test?
Are credentials distinct per environment?
heuristics.evidence: Data handling procedure for non-production and per-environment secret inventory.

heuristics.title: SBOM produced and consumed; dependency provenance known
heuristics.concern: Supply chain questions increasingly start with the SBOM and where components come from.
questions: Is an SBOM generated per release?
Which registries may components come from?
heuristics.evidence: Release SBOM and the dependency source policy.

heuristics.title: Documentation matches the deployed system
heuristics.concern: An assessor checks that the security plan describes the system as it actually runs, including its boundary.
questions: When was the system boundary diagram last verified against production?
Who owns keeping the plan current?
heuristics.evidence: Boundary diagram with a dated verification and change-control link.

heuristics.title: Administration is segregated and logged
heuristics.concern: Administrative paths that share the general network, or leave no log, are read as uncontrolled privilege.
questions: How do administrators reach production?
Where are administrative actions logged?
heuristics.evidence: Administration architecture and a sample of administrative audit logs.
